methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.skip_reason: insufficient narrow peer set in Drones & Autonomous (found 0 same-stage, 0 adjacent-stage, 0 similar-tier; need ≥3)
methods.rationale: 5 same-sector peers exist in Drones & Autonomous, but none of the narrow filters (same-stage / adjacent-stage / similar-valuation-tier) yielded ≥3 datapoints. Falling back to all-sector median would be misleading.

data.narrative:
Airship Industries is a seed-stage company in the Drones & Autonomous sector. The broader sector contains seven private companies tracked as peers, including Zipline, Joby Aviation, Nuro, Archer Aviation, and Elroy Air. No public comparables exist in this subsector, limiting the peer universe to private late-stage and growth-stage operators.

Standard peer-median valuation methodology is not applicable here. While five same-sector peers exist, none meet the narrow filtering criteria of matching stage, adjacent stage, or similar valuation tier simultaneously. Applying an all-sector median would introduce substantial cross-stage bias given the heterogeneity in development risk and capital requirements within Drones & Autonomous. The absence of same-stage or adjacent-stage datapoints precludes reliable triangulation via this method.

Without sufficient narrowly-defined peer data, this analysis cannot support a single point estimate or quantified range. Additional information—including revenue or funding metrics from comparable seed-stage drone companies, or alternative valuation signals such as grant funding, customer pipelines, or technology IP valuations—would be required to establish a defensible valuation floor or ceiling. The key uncertainty is the lack of near-peer staging data. Further due diligence on market-specific benchmarks or venture fund check sizes for this subsector may provide secondary anchors.
